programme.title: TOTP2
programme.desc: Top of the Pops 2 dips into the archives to explore both classic collective hits and smash solo singles spanning 20 early years of Genesis history. From the art-rock Gabriel era of flamboyant theatrics and quirky costumes to their eighties evolution into pop superstars, Genesis are both influential experimentalists and a chart-smashing behemoth. With solo numbers from Peter Gabriel, Phil Collins and Mike + The Mechanics, this is an eclectic two-sided playlist featuring everything from I Can't Dance to I Know What I Like, No Self Control to In the Air Tonight, and Many Too Many to The Living Years. So Turn It On Again and tune in, from prog to pop, Genesis to Revelation, the hits are here on TOTP2.

programme.title: Life on Earth
programme.desc: Some 350 million years ago, evolution reached one of its most crucial stages when fish crawled from the water onto the land and became amphibians. Today, newts, salamanders, toads and frogs still survive in great quantities, and there is even one species of frog where the male gives birth from its mouth! Presented by David Attenborough.

programme.title: Voyages of Discovery
programme.desc: Explorer Paul Rose tells the story of three Frenchmen who couldn't stand each other, yet set off on an eight-year scientific mission in one of the most hostile places on the planet. Their plan, to settle an international row by measuring the shape of the planet, took them to the disease-ridden rainforests and oxygen-starved peaks of the Ecuadorian Andes. Rose follows in the footsteps of the 18th-century explorers who were complete innocents abroad and had no idea of the horrors they were letting themselves in for. Despite disease, death and some highly disastrous sexual liaisons, the men made discoveries that fundamentally changed all our lives.

programme.title: The Sentinels
programme.desc: Irène follows a lead into a case involving Mirreau, who appears to be linked to a state secret. Meanwhile at Les Damnés, the Baron discovers that Gisèle has fled. After the tragic death of one of his brothers in arms, Gabriel wants to return to Paris to see his wife and son. In French and German with English subtitles.

programme.title: The Sentinels
programme.desc: The Sentinels must free Mazauric, the brain behind the Dyxenal research, before he divulges critical information about the French serum to the German forces. Meanwhile, the Baron receives a visit at his club from Diane, a German spy who pledges to find Gisèle in exchange for a favour. In French and German with English subtitles.

programme.title: Monster
programme.desc: When schoolboy Minato begins exhibiting strange behaviours, his mother, Sairo, suspects bullying by his teacher and confronts the school. The headmistress seems to be hiding something, and as Sairo pushes for answers, they turn out to be stranger than she imagined. In Japanese with English subtitles.

programme.title: Keeping Up Appearances
programme.desc: Hyacinth realises that Richard is bored after taking early retirement and provides him with a hobby - being artistic with a video camera. However, it's a decision she will live to regret.

programme.title: One Foot in the Grave

programme.title: Timeshift
programme.desc: Paul Atterbury embarks on an alluring journey into the golden age of ocean liners, finding out how these great ships made such a mark on the popular imagination and why they continue to enchant to this day. Paul's voyage takes him around Britain and reveals a story of design, politics, propaganda, Hollywood glamour and tragedy. Along the way, he uncovers some amazing survivals from the liners of the past - a cinema in Scotland built from the interiors of the SS Homeric, a house in Poole in which cabins from the Mauretania are lovingly preserved - as well as the design inspiration behind the first great liners.

programme.title: BBC Proms
programme.desc: The Sinfonia of London transcend in a programme brimming with colourful orchestration under the baton of their ever-popular artistic director, John Wilson. Opening with Verdi’s thunderous overture to La Forza del Destino, followed by Norwegian cellist Jonathan Aasgaard in his Proms soloist debut with Walton’s hypnotic Cello Concerto and finishing with the music time capsule that is Respighi’s enchanting sun-drenched Roman Trilogy. Presented by Katie Derham from the Royal Albert Hall.

programme.title: Not I
programme.desc: Billie Whitelaw gives a tour de force performance as a mouth suspended in space in Samuel Beckett's play.

programme.title: Performance
programme.desc: Michael Gambon stars in John Osborne's play, set in 1950s Britain, following Archie Rice, a drunken, lecherous, egotistical vaudevillian, whose act is on the downward slope.

programme.title: The Levin Interviews
programme.desc: Bernard Levin talks to playwright and screenwriter John Osborne, best known for his 1956 work Look Back in Anger.

programme.title: Searching for Sam: Adrian Dunbar on Samuel Beckett
programme.desc: Samuel Beckett has fascinated Adrian Dunbar since he was a young student. Thirty years after Beckett's death in Paris, Dunbar explores what made the man who wrote Waiting for Godot.

programme.title: Turtle, Eagle, Cheetah: A Slow Odyssey
programme.desc: Ride on board with a green sea turtle as it swims around its spectacular coral reef home of Sipidan in Malaysia. Using only natural sounds and elegant embedded graphics delivering detailed information, this is an immersive journey into the turtles’ world like no other. The turtle embarks on its daily routine, revealing how they utilise all the different areas of the reef, from the inner shallows to the deep drop-off – introducing us to all the fish and animals that they share one of the richest and most diverse places on our planet with in a mesmerising half-hour. The turtles were filmed for Blue Planet II and part of an ongoing study into their behaviour for the Marine Research Foundation.

programme.title: Atlantic: The Wildest Ocean on Earth
programme.desc: In the vast South Atlantic, huge pods of dolphins, massive penguin colonies and the largest gathering of marine mammals on earth pack chains of extraordinary islands, created by powerful volcanic forces far below them. Nutrient-rich upwellings create profusions of life in some areas, whilst extreme isolation and abyssal depths host a world of bizarre creatures in others.

programme.title: Treasures of Ancient Greece
programme.desc: Alastair Sooke explores the extraordinary afterlife of the Greek masterpieces that changed the course of western culture. Succeeding centuries have found in ancient Greek art inspiration for their own ideals and ambitions. Filming in Italy, Germany, France and Britain, Alastair's investigation includes The Venus of Knidos, the first naked woman in western art, the bronze horses of St Mark's in Venice which became a pawn in an imperial game, and the naked discus thrower, the Discobolus, personally bought by Adolf Hitler and used by him as a symbol of Aryan supremacy.

programme.title: Egypt's Lost Cities
programme.desc: It is possible that only one per cent of the wonders of ancient Egypt have been discovered, but now, thanks to a pioneering approach to archaeology, that is about to change. Dr Sarah Parcak uses satellites to probe beneath the sands, where she has found cities, temples and pyramids. Now, with Dallas Campbell and Liz Bonnin, she heads to Egypt to discover if these magnificent buildings are really there.

programme.title: Becoming Frida Kahlo
programme.desc: Frida and Diego travel to San Francisco, where he has an important mural commission. Frida's style stirs much excitement, and she is determined to succeed in her own right in the face of Diego's affairs. Shocked by the vast gap between rich and poor that she witnesses in Depression-era New York, she struggles to hide her disdain for high society. After losing a child to miscarriage and her mother to illness, she produces some of her most visceral and devastating works.

programme.title: Leonardo
programme.desc: She has her own bodyguards and lives in Paris in a humidified, air-conditioned box protected by triplex bulletproof glass. Despite this, she is visited by six million tourists every year. She is Leonardo da Vinci's Mona Lisa. Alan Yentob tells the story of how the Mona Lisa came to be the most famous work of art in the world. It's a tale full of notoriety, glamour and intrigue as the Mona Lisa is abducted, vandalised and exploited across the centuries. With the help of leading scholars and original research, Alan also finally solves the central mystery of the Mona Lisa - who she is and why she is smiling.

programme.desc: A global programme that reflects the variety of takes on climate change, how best to understand it and the world's attempts to avert it, temper it or adapt to it. programme.title: The Media Show
programme.desc: An AI-generated actor called Tilly Norwood has been cast in the lead role of a forthcoming film, adding to the debate about artificial intelligence in filmmaking. The announcement follows criticism from actors such as Emily Blunt, and objections from the US performers' union. Eline Van der Velden, founder and CEO of Particle6, explains why she created Tilly Norwood, while Jake Kanter, international investigations editor at Deadline, sets out the reaction from the film industry. Andy Burnham has become the UK's new prime minister, and his approach to the media is already attracting attention. His team has relied more on social media, online creators and direct communication than on traditional broadcast interviews. Lizzy Buchan, political editor of the Daily Mirror; Jennifer Gerber, senior political advisor, WA Communications; Tom Nicholas, creator of the Slow News Day YouTube channel; and broadcaster Andrew Neil, presenter of The Andrew Neil Report, assess what this could mean for political journalism and public accountability.

programme.title: The Travel Show
programme.desc: It's an important year for the city of Hull, in northern England. It's celebrating more than 800 years of maritime history with a raft of new museum openings that it's hoped will make it a world-class visitor attraction. Emeline Nsingi Nkosi goes to see the opening of the restored Spurn Lightship - literally a lighthouse on a ship - which was a mainstay on the waterways there for 50 years. She meets the people involved in the huge regeneration effort and finds out why the city's been the punchline of jokes for so many years.

programme.title: Talking Business
programme.desc: Just how long can Iran afford to keep fighting the US? War is expensive, and Iran's economy is facing recession as people struggle with soaring prices, rising unemployment and a weak currency. But with the fighting continuing, are years of international financial sanctions really having the desired impact? Professor Djavad Salehi-Isfahani, a leading expert on Iran's economy, tells us what he found on a recent visit to Tehran, and Mark Wallace, CEO of campaign group United Against a Nuclear Iran, explains the realities of sanctions. Plus, Ben Thompson also hears from Tom Broughton, founder of London glasses brand Cubitts, about how he's taking on the big names in a multi-billion dollar industry.

programme.title: China's Greatest Treasures
programme.desc: The Yellow River - running for almost five and half thousand kilometres from west to east - is known as China's mother river. It's hailed as the cradle of Chinese civilisation and over thousands of years, it has fed billions of people and inspired generations of artists. Alastair explores the Yellow River and discovers some of the finest artwork from its valley, to understand how this unique natural phenomenon is deeply connected with the identity of the Chinese and the roots of their culture.

programme.title: Prayer and Reflection
programme.desc: Nottingham Liberal Synagogue, part of the Progressive Judaism movement, guide us into the Sabbath with their musical Friday evening service, known as Erev Shabbat. Led by Rabbi Gili Zidkiyahu alongside co-Rabbi Josh Levy, this inclusive musical service welcomes all members of the community together to usher in the Sabbath. With liturgical guidance from our prayer leaders, the service blends ancient psalms and prayers, including the Sh’ma (prayer and declaration of faith) and a silent Amidah (offering time for personal reflection) with poetry and hymns. After the blessing of the challah, a traditional Jewish bread, and the Kiddush (sanctification of the wine), the community enjoy a light bring-and-share supper in the synagogue and talk about what being part of the Progressive Judaism movement means to them.

programme.title: Pilgrimage
programme.desc: Seven celebrities of differing faiths and beliefs experience an emotional journey on a pilgrimage in north Wales, a route linked by churches dedicated to early Celtic Christian saints. Immersing themselves on this spiritual journey are wildlife presenter Michaela Strachan, who places her faith in the natural world; Spencer Matthews, a former Made in Chelsea reality star who was christened in the Church of England but is still searching for answers to life’s big questions; Sonali Shah, a journalist and TV presenter who grew up in a Jain family; comedian Eshaan Akbar, a lapsed Muslim; Amanda Lovett, a practising Catholic who was catapulted into the public eye in the first series of Traitors; actor Tom Rosenthal of Friday Night Dinner fame, who is areligious; and TV personality and former model Christine McGuinness, who is spiritual but doesn’t practise one particular faith. Travelling on foot and by bus, the seven pilgrims begin their adventure at Flint Castle on the bank of the Dee Estuary and follow the coastal path to Greenfield Valley, the official start of the 220km Pilgrim’s Way.

programme.title: Money for Nothing

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: The final stop on Anita’s east coast road trip is the mysterious Orford Ness in Suffolk. Once a top-secret military testing facility, this ten-mile shingle spit is now one of Britain's most important protected coastal landscapes, where former military buildings provide nesting sites for seabirds. Anita explores the abandoned military complex to uncover Orford Ness's secretive past and discovers how a landscape once shaped by weapons testing has been reclaimed by wildlife. She also meets an artist inspired to write an album about the area’s fascinating past and its current status as a nature haven. Along the way, Anita looks back through the Countryfile archives at the communities exposed to the sea and how nature can stage a comeback.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: The roadshow is at Sefton Park in Liverpool, where Chinese ceramics expert Lars Tharp sees a rare double Ming dynasty vase bought in a charity shop, Raj Bisram discovers some valuable Beatles memorabilia, and Dendy Easton admires a painting by George Melly. Expert Ronnie Archer-Morgan is almost tricked by an intriguing Grand Tour bronze, Andy McConnell falls in love with some unusual Finnish glass, and Raj is excited to see a silver disc brought in by one of the members of Gerry and the Pacemakers. Will Farmer challenges Fiona Bruce to guess the values of three vases by pioneering female artists, and Fiona discovers the history behind the famous Palm House in Sefton Park.

programme.title: The Rapture
programme.desc: Child psychologist Dr Gabrielle 'Gabs' Fox is recovering from the trauma of a car accident that killed her husband, Alex, and left her paralysed. Grieving and guilt-ridden, she has moved to the coastal town of Porth Hen in South Wales and is slowly learning to rebuild her life with the help of her own psychologist, Mel. Gabs accepts a position at Oxsmith Psychiatric Hospital, where she is assigned several new patients, including the unit’s most disturbed patient, 17-year-old Bethany Krall. Dangerous, intelligent and manipulative, Bethany was sectioned two years ago for the brutal murder of her mother, Carys Krall. The crime shocked the nation, not least because Bethany’s bereft father, Leonard Krall, is the charismatic leader of the Faith Way, a feelgood religious movement boasting millions of followers thanks to its reassuring motto 'Choose Hope'. But when Gabs reads Bethany’s case file, she finds the previous psychologist left very few notes.

programme.desc: Ben Fogle and Kate Humble are back at Longleat, Britain’s first safari park, where life never stands still and neither do the challenges. As the park prepares for its first hippos in over 40 years, a heartbreaking battle unfolds in Lion Country. The keepers are on high alert as Malaika, the beloved matriarch of the pride, shows worrying signs of illness. If the other lions sense her weakness, they could turn on her, with devastating consequences. Meanwhile, Ben helps with a high-stakes mission to outwit the park’s notorious macaques before they dismantle their latest enrichment challenge. Hamza faces his own test as he tries to distinguish the youngest members of the ostrich flock, vital work if any bird needs urgent care. And Megan meets a red panda for an ingenious health check, while deep in the park’s wilderness, the beavers are reshaping the land, but will their hard work survive human interference?

programme.title: Trace, Track, Get My Car Back
programme.desc: Criminals often use hire cars whilst carrying out their illegal activities. By constantly switching vehicles, they make it harder for the police to trace crimes back to them. A Land Rover hired out by a rental company has been linked to a spate of street robberies in Manchester. The car is now 200 miles away in central London, but it’s fitted with a tracker, so Neil and his team are following its every move. As they close in on the suspect vehicle, they call for police back-up and prepare to swoop. In the UK, over 300 vehicles are stolen every day, and many of them are shipped overseas, where they are sold to unscrupulous buyers. But the authorities are fighting back against organised gangs of car thieves smuggling stolen vehicles out of the country through ports such as Felixstowe. In just a few hours, stolen vehicle examiner Adam discovers six cars, worth around £200,000, hidden inside shipping containers and about to be exported. Cars aren’t the only vehicles to be targeted by criminals. In Nottingham, thieves have made off with a three-tonne digger. But it’s fitted with a tracking device, so Richard hits the road, determined to find it and get it back off the thieves.

With antiques expert Jonathan Pratt by their side, the reds weigh up a set of brass and wrought iron scales, which appeal to former blacksmith Phil. For the sale, the teams travel to Buckinghamshire, where Hugo Lemon gives his auctioneer estimates on their purchases, and for one duo, their bonus buy is definitely worth writing home about.

Things get complicated when a classmate of Aks's, Ridwan, makes some very unwise decisions that leave Mobeen very concerned. Eight, meanwhile, is in danger of getting in too deep with a local wide boy, and he is potentially going to drag everyone down with him. Can Mobeen manage to keep everyone out of trouble?

programme.title: Man Like Mobeen
programme.desc: When Aks breaks her shoulder and heads for hospital with the boys, Accident and Emergency is the state of play. With Mobeen, Eight and Nate looking shifty de facto, the authorities start to get suspicious about how Aks may have sustained her injuries. In the waiting room, we see life in an overstretched A&E and the gang in a constant battle to prove their innocence, battle prejudice and, of course, keep Pakistani Rain Man (Eight) out of trouble.

programme.title: Man Like Mobeen
programme.desc: They say the past is never far away. And for Mobeen, it’s about to punch him in the throat. Cal, an old friend, makes an unexpected return to Small Heath, leaving Aks, Eight and Nate very concerned about what this means for Mobeen. Can he stay clear of trouble, or are things about to take a turn for the worse?

programme.title: Man Like Mobeen
programme.desc: Dogs and ethnic minorities have a very bad track record. So when a clip involving Mobeen and an Alsatian goes viral, it’s a disaster. Aks is drawn in by the prospect of internet fame, while Mobeen tries to see if the spark between him and Aks’s teacher, Miss Aitken, is worth pursuing. The past finally catches up with our hero, though, leaving him with some very difficult decisions to make. Our season finale will change the game forever.

programme.title: Grime Kids
programme.desc: School’s out. Dane, Junior, Bishop, and Bayo want to make the most of their summer. Dane’s old friend Kai has an idea about how. Armed with fake IDs and fake bravado, they sneak in to Knights of the Realm, the rave of the summer. The boys are awestruck by the wall-to-wall designer labels, the famous faces, the music, and the girls - one girl in particular for Dane (and Kai).

programme.title: Grime Kids
programme.desc: Historical tensions simmer, but Dane focuses on his plans for the garage crew - newly named 'Gladiators... because Roman Road.' With little to no money (and talent), they’re not sure where to start. When Kai feels excluded from the group and jealous over Dane’s relationship with Genevieve, tensions boil over. Bishop makes friends with Donnie, drawn to his flashy wealth and lifestyle.

programme.title: Grime Kids
programme.desc: The boys support Junior at his mum’s memorial service, and Junior worries his dad is hiding a secret from him. Dane’s love life starts to become more serious as the Gladiator Crew sign up to compete against other crews in a music competition, where a cash prize and a free studio session are up for grabs. Bayo’s sister tells him she has a meeting with a pirate radio DJ.

programme.title: BBC New Comedy Awards
programme.desc: The BBC’s big comedy talent search heads to Northern Ireland and the capital, Belfast, where five hopefuls will battle it out to book their place in Birmingham for the grand final showdown. This show comes from the MAC, an award-winning venue in Belfast’s Cathedral Quarter, which is home to all kinds of theatre performances, comedy and music gigs. Since opening in 2012, the MAC has become a beacon for the ongoing regeneration of Belfast. Comedian, author and the creator of online sensation Mammy Banter, Serena Terry, is our host. Joining her is comedian and former New Comedy Awards alumnus Vittorio Angelone, BBC head of development for comedy commissioning Roya Eslami, and the head honcho, Babatunde Aleshe. The judges will have their work cut out picking a winner from the five comics. Ciaran Franco, Adam Perrott, Marty Gleeson, Bert Broadbent and Mark Moloney all take to the stage with sets that are jam-packed with fresh material and jokes a plenty.

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: Steve Backshall's journey is almost over; he only needs two more animals to complete his Deadly 60 list. It is a tough choice and Steve is in the rainforests of Brazil on the trail of the final contenders. The place is teeming with wildlife, not to mention some seriously large spiders, but Steve is after a monster tarantula for his list. Deep in the jungle at night, Steve and the team witness one of the most amazing spectacles of the series as they encounter a colony of army ants on the move.

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: Steve Backshall has encountered some incredible animals on his search around the planet for his Deadly 60. All the animals that made it onto Steve's list are deadly in their own right, but a handful of them are deadly to humans. This programme looks at those animals in detail, dispelling myths and showing just how incredible they truly are.

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: The Great British Sewing Bee returns with brand new host Sophie Willan. Over ten weeks, 12 of the country’s best home sewers compete to be crowned winner of the Sewing Bee crown. In the opening week, judges Patrick Grant and Esme Young set three challenges on the theme of the British summer. First up, the Pattern Challenge sees them crafting summer shorts with a patch pocket. Next, in the 90-minute Transformation Challenge, barbecue aprons become bags. Finally, there is a Sewing Bee first in the Made-to-Measure Challenge as the sewers are asked to create garments to fit themselves. They become their own models as they make outfits for their ideal summer’s day, and once complete, the catwalk is all theirs. One sewer will impress and earn Garment of the Week, but for another, it’s the end of the road as they leave the sewing room for good.

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: It’s week 2, and judges Patrick Grant and Esme Young put the 11 remaining sewers through their paces with three challenges themed around prints and colours. First, the sewers take on the Pattern Challenge, constructing a pattern-matched shell top with adaptive elements, including invisible side-zips and a high-low hem. In the Transformation Challenge, they are given second-hand clothes in purple and brown, the judges’ least-favourite colours, and have to create garments that will convince them to change their minds. Finally, in the Made-to-Measure, the sewers must create an eye-catching outfit in just one colour.

programme.desc: Mia (Emma Stone), an aspiring actress, and Sebastian (Ryan Gosling), a dedicated jazz musician, fall in love while struggling to make ends meet in a city known for crushing hopes and breaking hearts. Set in modern-day Los Angeles, this award-winning musical about everyday life explores the joy and pain of pursuing your dreams.

programme.title: Things You Should Have Done
programme.desc: Shock horror when Chi discovers bills are a thing, and her electricity and water get cancelled. As a result, she decides she's just going to live at auntie Karen's.

programme.title: Things You Should Have Done
programme.desc: Chi organises a family camping holiday to help Karen relax, since she was 'diagnosed uptight' and told she’s unlikely to get pregnant if she doesn’t lower her blood pressure.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: It’s the first ever RHS Sandringham Flower Show, and Arit Anderson, Jamie Butterworth and Frances Tophill are on hand to take a look around. From spectacular show gardens to a floral marquee packed full of horticultural goodies, there is something to whet the appetite. A local grower who knows everything there is to know about roses provides expert advice, while a National Collection holder in Lincolnshire shines a light on drought-tolerant achilleas. A couple in Kent share their new-found love of succulents, with some useful advice on how to care for them. And in Hampshire, a plantsman conveys his passion for carrying on the family tradition of running a nursery.

programme.title: This Wild Life
programme.desc: Wildlife expert Saba Douglas-Hamilton, together with her husband Frank and their three young children, move to the romantic Samburu National Reserve in Kenya to run a safari camp for the first time. But life out there isn't easy. There are monkeys in the kitchen, floods threatening the camp and, with no fences to keep out the wildlife, elephants are regular house guests. This series follows their ups and downs as the family struggles to keep guests, elephants, lions and even crocodiles smiling. Wildlife expert Saba Douglas-Hamilton and the elephant rescue team race to save the life of a recently orphaned calf. The baby elephant is flown to an elephant orphanage in Nairobi. But with a terror threat on the Kenya's east coast, the family's safari camp is in crisis. Saba must work to save the business and do all she can to try to protect Samburu's trusting elephants.

programme.title: Funeral in Berlin
programme.desc: Harry Palmer is sent to Berlin with instructions to assist Colonel Stok, the Russian head of security for the Berlin Wall, who is eager to defect to the West. However, Palmer discovers he cannot trust anyone in the city where the double-cross is a unit of currency.

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: It’s week 2, and judges Patrick Grant and Esme Young put the 11 remaining sewers through their paces with three challenges themed around prints and colours. First, the sewers take on the Pattern Challenge, constructing a pattern-matched shell top with adaptive elements, including invisible side-zips and a high-low hem. In the Transformation Challenge, they are given second-hand clothes in purple and brown, the judges’ least-favourite colours, and have to create garments that will convince them to change their minds. Finally, in the Made-to-Measure, the sewers must create an eye-catching outfit in just one colour.

programme.title: High Society
programme.desc: Musical comedy. Time is short if playboy CK Dexter-Haven is to reclaim his former wife before she remarries. Cynical reporter Mike Connor is covering the wedding.

programme.title: Casablanca
programme.desc: Classic romantic drama. Rick's Cafe is a centre for criminals, refugees, resistance fighters and Nazis. Its cynical owner takes risks for no-one - until the arrival of Ilsa.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: This time, Flog It! comes from the RAF Museum in Cosford, Shropshire. Antiques experts Adam Partridge and Claire Rawle are on hand to find a selection of objects to take to auction. Claire gets sentimental over a music box and Adam discovers a silver cigarette case from Russia. Paul Martin falls for an iconic bike and visits the nearby historic Ironbridge to investigate the start of the industrial revolution.

programme.title: Rugby League: Super League
programme.desc: Coverage from the Super League as Leigh Leopards take on Warrington Wolves.

programme.title: Evolution
programme.desc: How did the ostrich come to lay the biggest egg on earth? Chris Packham explores the way reproduction has shaped life on earth and the surprising evolutionary origins of sex, eggs and birds. It's a four-billion-year journey contained within a shell.

programme.title: Bonnie Tyler at the BBC
programme.desc: A celebration of the incredible 50-year career of Bonnie Tyler, the only Welsh performer to have a US number one. Bonnie's distinctive husky vocals and powerful performances made her one of Britain's best-loved and most enduring artists. This collection from the BBC archive showcases some of her biggest and best moments from over the decades, with hits including Lost in France, Holding Out for a Hero, It's a Heartache and the song frequently voted the greatest power ballad in pop history, Total Eclipse of the Heart.

programme.title: Top of the Pops
programme.desc: Revel in many of the biggest singles of 2002 as the Top of the Pops archives are opened once again. P!nk gets the party started, and there are hits from Shakira, Sugababes and Atomic Kitten. The Red Hot Chili Peppers are back alongside Oasis and Kelly Rowland with her first major release after leaving Destiny’s Child. Also, the TV talent show introduces Will Young with the biggest selling track of the year. Featuring P!nk, The Coral, Shakira, Liberty X, DJ Sammy and Yanou and Do, Oasis, Will Young, Sugababes, Nelly and Kelly Rowland, Atomic Kitten, Red Hot Chili Peppers, Avril Lavigne, Daniel Bedingfield, Badly Drawn Boy, Holly Valance, Elvis vs JXL, Ja Rule and Ashanti, Girls Aloud and Enrique Iglesias.

programme.title: Top of the Pops
programme.desc: A look back at a year where Top of the Pops comes under attack from the TV talent show and girl groups are back at the top. 2002 sees the return of Sugababes 2.0, the chart domination of talent show winners (and losers), as well as the cultural phenomenon which is Vanessa Carlton with that piano riff. Meanwhile, Swedish band The Hives arrive at Television Centre, whilst indie rock continues its early 00s climb of the chart. With 2,000 episodes under its belt, TOTP is more diverse and dominant than ever before. Contributors include Mutya and Keisha from Sugababes, Kimberly Walsh from Girls Aloud, Vanessa Carlton, Liberty X, The Hives, Frankie Bridge from S Club Juniors, Gareth Gates and broadcasters Trevor Nelson, Pete Tong and Sarah Cawood.

programme.title: Top of the Pops
programme.desc: An exclusive set from the Red Hot Chili Peppers, performed in front of Television Centre, comprising old and new songs. From 2006.

programme.title: Girls Aloud at the BBC
programme.desc: They first triumphed on the 2002 reality show Pop Stars: The Rivals, and over the next decade, dominated the UK charts, the tabloids and the affections of fans of pure pop perfection. Here are the group’s greatest musical moments and biggest hits, from their chart-topping debut Sound of the Underground to Something Kind of Ooooh, Can’t Speak French, Call the Shots and beyond.

programme.title: Coldplay: Best of the BBC
programme.desc: Coldplay fans will be in Paradise with this trip through the BBC’s archives, which follows the incredible journey that’s taken the band from promising new talents, whose first hits coincided with the start of a new century, right through to stadium-filling global superstars. With all the key songs and anthems taken from a selection of their finest TV performances, this Coldplay mix looks and sounds Magic.

programme.title: Who Do You Think You Are?
programme.desc: Toby Jones explores an extraordinary acting dynasty on his mum’s side, and he is determined to discover whether his dad’s stories of a connection to India are fact or fiction.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: The A to Z of TV Gardening
programme.desc: Carol Kirkwood takes an alphabetical journey through the world of gardening, getting inspiration and advice from some of the BBC's most popular garden presenters and programmes. In this episode, she's exploring subjects that all begin with the letter Q. Programmes include Gardeners' World, The One Show, RHS Chelsea Flower Show and Springwatch, with presenters Monty Don, Chris Packham, Joe Swift, James Alexander Sinclair, Alan Titchmarsh, Nicky Chapman, Andy Sturgeon and Carol Klein.

programme.title: Glorious Gardens from Above
programme.desc: Christine Walkden heads for the lakes and fells of Cumbria to visit some more magnificent gardens. At Levens Hall, she lends a hand planting some spring bulbs and hears some of lakeland lad Len's special memories. At Holehird, she meets the dedicated volunteers who have restored this 19th-century garden to its former glory. And we discover the spur to Beatrix Potter's prolific writing career.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Anita continues her east coast road trip, visiting the Naze, a nature reserve on the Essex coast. Here, coastal erosion is particularly severe, with around 2 to 3 metres lost from the cliffs every year. But there are benefits to a crumbling coastline – it can reveal 55 million years of history. Anita joins a group of enthusiastic fossil hunters on the lookout for remnants of the coast's fascinating past. She also discovers what has been done to protect the area’s heritage and visits one of over a thousand brightly coloured beach huts overlooking the North Sea. Along the way, Anita looks back through the Countryfile archives at the hidden histories found across our landscape.

programme.title: Weatherman Walking
programme.desc: Derek revisits three walks that have changed people’s lives. He sees how the great outdoors aided a cancer patient’s recovery and inspired those with sight loss to go birdwatching.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: It's all about the borders at Beechgrove Garden as Brian Cunningham and Kirsty Wilson replant, fill gaps and replace losses all around the plot. Kirsty revisits her hot border, designed to display vibrant colours at the height of summer. The winter temperatures killed off a few plants, so she will be trying out some alternatives. Brian is in the calendar border, created to have some form of colour or interest every month of the year. It has not had much attention this year, so Brian will be topping it up to ensure year-round performance. Kirsty will also be planting in the border behind Beechgrove's main pond, where other gaps have appeared, and she is building a new structure to create a habitat for pollinators. There is a trip to visit a great garden on the Cowal Peninsula, and all the week's handy hints.

programme.title: Saturday Kitchen Best Bites
programme.desc: Matt Tebbutt brings the sunshine to the menu with a riot of summertime recipes. Hasan Semay celebrates Turkish mezze with a quartet of outstanding dishes – hummus with chopped salad, atom peppers, deep-fried calamari and bulgur wheat salad. Freddy Bird roasts Iberico pork chops, served with a rich butcher’s sauce, buttery mashed potato and spring greens. Anna Haugh puts Irish cuisine in the spotlight with her balsamic prawns with creamy polenta. And Dr Saliha Mahmood Ahmed has a classic Indian street food snack, aloo bun chaat, and a side of refreshing pani puri. Olly Smith has a whirlwind tour of cheese and wine pairings, and Johannes Radebe tucks into either his food heaven, Thai fried rice with fried chicken, or his food hell, chilled courgette soup. Meanwhile, Rick Stein is on the hunt for the best-tasting carrots, and the Hairy Bikers explore Catalan influences in Italy.

programme.title: Indian Food Made Easy
programme.desc: Food writer and chef Anjum Anand is on a mission to show novice cooks how to cook simple yet delicious Indian food. In this episode she takes a stall at the quintessentially English Sherborne Country Fair where she hopes to persuade the masses to ditch greasy burgers and hot dogs in favour of her healthier alternative, and raise money for charity. She enlists the help of energetic friend Panthea, who is a great sales woman but can't cook, so Anjum decides it is time for her to learn. Anjum shows Panthea how to cook up a tandoori-style feast. There is delicious chicken tikka marinated in ginger, garlic, spices and yoghurt, before being grilled and served in a wrap with crunchy salad. Plus luscious lamb brochettes with a mint and coriander pickle. For the vegetarians, thick tandoori mushrooms with a spinach, peanut and paneer filling. All that is left is for Panthea to master the art of making samosas and the two head off to Dorset to see if they are a match for the burger vans.

programme.title: Indian Food Made Easy
programme.desc: Alex, a friend of Anjum Anand's, is having the boys over to watch the FA Cup Final. His initial thought is an Indian takeaway, but Anjum persuades him to cook up an Indian feast. Having treated him to a tasty breakfast of mango smoothies, they head to the supermarket to pick up ingredients where Alex learns everything there is to know about chillies. Anjum and Alex make spicy lamb burgers made with fresh chillies, ginger, mint and lashings of coriander as well as delicious chilli-chicken - rolled in bread crumbs and oven-baked. Anjum then reveals the ancient art of cheese-making before visiting a top Indian restaurant in London where Head Chef Mehernosh shows her the secrets of kulfi, a rich Indian ice cream.

programme.title: Operation Crossbow
programme.desc: World War II drama. A small group of agents is sent on a vital mission to destroy a Nazi V-2 rocket base in Holland. Their aim is to prevent flying bombs from falling on London.

programme.title: Cricket: The Hundred
programme.desc: Coverage of The Hundred 100-ball cricket tournament.

programme.title: Cricket: The Hundred
programme.desc: Coverage of The Hundred 100-ball cricket tournament.

programme.title: Live at the Apollo
programme.desc: This episode of the series is hosted by quick-witted Dara O Briain, who introduces wonderful Australian comic Felicity Ward and the sensational Mo Gilligan to the stage.

programme.title: Taxi Driver
programme.desc: Travis Bickle is an alienated ex-Marine, working nights as a New York cabbie. Haunted by the squalor around him, he is drawn to the beautiful - and 'pure' - Betsy, but his attempts to woo her prove disastrous, and he begins a descent into a personal hell. Cult drama directed by Martin Scorsese and scripted by Paul Schrader.

programme.title: The Elephant Man
programme.desc: In 1884, an ambitious young surgeon is intrigued by a sideshow freak billed as the Elephant Man. He finds, behind the disfigured exhibit, an intelligent person whose rehabilitation he undertakes.

programme.title: Do You Know Your Place?
programme.desc: Comedian and presenter Susan Calman, internet star Max Fosh and DJ Noreen Khan have to separate unbelievable facts from playful fiction. Vernon Kay hosts as unreliable tour guide Paul Gorton shares the sights and stories of Abergavenny as the week reaches its midpoint.

programme.title: Ann Droid
programme.desc: Sue isn’t thrilled that Michael is back with Renee, his cheating wife, and turns down an invite to Renee’s BJJ graduation ceremony, pretending she has other plans and upsetting Michael in the process. Sue doesn’t have any plans, so offers to work in the charity shop to help out Eileen, but it’s a disaster. Sue realises she should go and support Michael after all and prove she’s still a good mum, but Linda causes chaos.

programme.title: The Devil in the Family: The Fall of Ruby Franke
programme.desc: Millions watch Ruby Franke’s wholesome YouTube content, but happy families are rarely as they seem. Could life coach Jodi Hildebrandt hold the answers to the family’s problems?

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Eric Knowles meets a collector with a thirst for preserving brewery history. In a converted garage in Nottinghamshire, Richard Percival has 1,300 beer trays, dating back more than 100 years. Made of heavy steel with ornate designs, they’re all striking examples of British advertising – and Eric Knowles has arranged a surprise visit for him, to recognise his record-breaking collection! In nearby Newark, two teams hope their items will serve up a profit when they go shopping with their antiques experts. Nick Hall is browsing bargains with the reds, Gary and Ian, and Izzie Balmer is with the blues, Joe and Hazel. With 60 minutes on the clock, the red team spots a pot with a rim made by a well-known silversmith and decide it’s one to think about. Meanwhile, the blues are mixing things up with a pestle and mortar. In Derbyshire, it’s almost time for last orders as auctioneer Charles Hanson gets the bids flowing.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: Kate Humble and Ben Fogle celebrate 25 years together on Animal Park, looking back at some of the animals, keepers and unforgettable moments they have shared, while new stories continue to unfold across the park. It's an emotional time in Wolf Wood as beloved male wolf Terry falls seriously ill. Faced with a heartbreaking decision, the keepers say goodbye to him, leaving his mate Meg alone just as she may be carrying his pups. Days later, when Meg disappears into her den and refuses to emerge, fears grow for her safety and the future of Terry's legacy. As part of the anniversary celebrations, Ben and Kate look back at one of the park's most memorable stories, the ingenious homemade wheel that transformed the life of three-legged tortoise Winky and captured the hearts of viewers. Elsewhere, Kate catches up with the park's new hippos as they continue settling into their purpose-built home, while Megan puts some of the park's longest tongues to the test and joins the rhino keepers for an up-close health check.

programme.title: The Repair Shop
programme.desc: The team revive a powered football wheelchair, some meticulously handcrafted jewellery, a bagatelle board, and a speedway flag that tells a remarkable Glaswegian love story.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week the celebrity contestants Yasmine Akram, Cariad Lloyd, Geoff Norcott and Dennis Taylor take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quick-fire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted by the House of Games kitchen composter?

programme.title: The Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp and his sidekick Sarah Greene host this quiz show where the contestants race on moving podiums across the studio floor. Correct answers get the players moving, while wrong answers stop them in their tracks. Five contestants battle across a series of fast-paced qualifiers and head-to-head races where the aim of the game is simple - make it to the finish line before your rivals. The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize.

programme.title: Lightning
programme.desc: Comedian Zoe Lyons presents the electrifyingly fast quiz with a £3,000 jackpot. Six plucky contestants compete across six rounds testing their general knowledge, quick thinking and speedy reactions whilst our ruthless spotlight patrols the studio. The contestants’ motivation in each round is simple: stay out of the light and you’ll be all right!

programme.title: Hairy Bikers' Bakeation
programme.desc: The Hairy Bikers start their epic 5,000-mile bakeation in Kristiansund on Norway's stunning west coast. They ride out along the Atlantic highway, ferry-hopping from island to island, and enjoy the thrilling biking provided by the spectacular roads that hug the rugged coastline of the fjords before arriving in the capital, Oslo, for the annual Norway Day celebrations. As they travel, they meet extraordinary artisan bakers, who are only too keen to teach them how to make their Norwegian specialities. They also meet some talented home-bakers, including 95-year-old Nikka, who rustles up waffles on her 65-year-old waffle iron. The Bikers choose amazing locations to cook some of their favourite Norwegian recipes: Scandinavian rye bread, cardamom and lemon cookies, and pirogi (ham- and Jarlsberg-filled pastries). On their travels, they taste the Norwegian delicacies of brown cheese and aquavit, Si rediscovers his Viking roots, and they both push themselves to the limit when they attempt the Olympic bobsleigh run.

programme.title: The Farmers' Country Showdown
programme.desc: Paul’s East Sussex smallholding is home to his two loves, his pigs and his family. Paul’s ten-year-old grandson Bobby is a regular visitor and helps him look after them. Paul is a self-confessed novice farmer, and this will be his and Bobby’s first time competing at Edenbridge & Oxted Agricultural Show. Besides the challenge of showing against much more experienced farmers, Paul runs the risk of his spirited Tamworths giving him the runaround in the ring. Meanwhile, Hannah, a sheep farmer from Kent, may have only been in the business for a few years, but she is serious about racking up some top rosettes with her Hampshire Down flock, even though she’s up against some of the best local breeders.

programme.title: Earth from Space
programme.desc: Cameras in space tell stories of life on our planet from a brand new perspective. Satellites follow an elephant family struggling through drought, reveal previously unknown emperor penguin colonies from the colour of their poo, and discover mysterious ice rings that could put seal pups in danger. Using cameras on the ground, in the air and in space, Earth from Space follows nature’s greatest spectacles, weather events and dramatic seasonal changes. This is our home, as we’ve never seen it before.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: In the spectacular setting of Gloucester Cathedral, presenter Paul Martin and experts Philip Serrell and Michael Baggott unearth some unusual items among the antiques and collectibles brought along to the valuation day. Philip discovers there are still bargains to be found at car boot sales, and an exquisite and valuable Italian micromosaic necklace sparks Michael's interest. Paul also fulfils a lifelong dream when he runs away to Gloucester-based circus Giffords and learns a few tricks of the trade from its famous clown Tweedy.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Karen Hauer, Storm Huntley, Joe Marler and Tom Read Wilson take on a series of rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games suitcase, or will they be tempted with the House of Games bee hotel?

programme.title: Just One Thing
programme.desc: Clive Myrie is in Kent with Tracey, a soon-to-be grandmother who is worried about her high blood pressure. His suggestion? Borrow a pet – yes, really. With new apps making it simple to match people with animals, Tracey could enjoy all the benefits without the long-term commitment. And the science is clear: spending time with animals boosts happiness, improves wellbeing and lowers the risk of dying from cardiovascular disease. A furry friend might be just what her heart needs.

programme.title: Global Eye
programme.desc: A weekly programme from the BBC World Service bringing forensic journalism from all corners of the world by BBC Eye, the World Service's critically acclaimed investigative unit, and featuring expert global correspondents getting to the heart of the biggest international stories. This week, BBC Eye talks to Ukrainians civilians abused in Russian-occupied Ukraine and tracks down the prison guards, officials and soldiers likely responsible. And Kurumi Mori explores a question now shaping the future of Japan: as the country relies more on foreign workers, can it embrace greater diversity without losing what it means to be Japanese?

programme.title: Mastermind
programme.desc: Clive Myrie presents another heat of the classic quiz where contenders take on the famous black chair under the glare of the spotlight and the ticking clock in an attempt to become the next Mastermind champion. The specialist subjects are the band Madness, Scottish geologist James Hutton, the films of Wes Anderson and the history of the Paris Metro.

programme.title: Only Connect
programme.desc: Victoria Coren Mitchell presides over the quiz where knowledge only gets you so far – the vital extra ingredients are logic and lateral thinking. It's Scotland versus Southport, with the teams clashing over such fiendish questions as: what would come fourth in the following sequence, 7: 1111111, 5: SEVEN, 3: VII…?

programme.title: University Challenge
programme.desc: In another first-round game, University College, Oxford play St John’s College, Cambridge. Amol Rajan asks the questions.

programme.title: Evolution
programme.desc: How did the bat get so hungry? Chris Packham sets out to answer a deceptively simple question: how the drive to find food shaped life on earth and gave rise to one of nature’s most insatiable feeders. This is the story of the origin of bums, guts, jaws and super hearing, and a 500-million-year chain of innovation, survival and hunger.

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Paul and Bob are in the Lake District to fish at some of the UK’s best-loved beauty spots – Derwentwater and Watendlath Tarn. In a change from the norm, this time Bob has chosen where they go fishing in a poignant trip down memory lane for him - this was where he used to come on camping holidays with his mates, away from parents for the first time.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Anita continues her east coast road trip, visiting the Naze, a nature reserve on the Essex coast. Here, coastal erosion is particularly severe, with around 2 to 3 metres lost from the cliffs every year. But there are benefits to a crumbling coastline – it can reveal 55 million years of history. Anita joins a group of enthusiastic fossil hunters on the lookout for remnants of the coast's fascinating past. She also discovers what has been done to protect the area’s heritage and visits one of over a thousand brightly coloured beach huts overlooking the North Sea. Along the way, Anita looks back through the Countryfile archives at the hidden histories found across our landscape.
